messages:
alex: heads-up — porting the embed-batcher helper from py -> ts sdk. running into 3 things at once, can anyone quick sanity-check?

1) auth refresh: token refresh sometimes yields 401 in the middle of a batch (we refresh per-batch). i saw it on a 256-item batch, halfway through requests start failing with 401. tokens look valid in the store.

2) dims weirdness: some inputs in the same batch are returning embeddings length 1537 while model is documented 1536. only happens for a few items, not reproducible locally.

3) streaming iterator: when we stream embeddings we get an extra empty vector "[]" at the end of the stream (breaks downstream dedupe).

any quickories? pinging @maria and @jonathan for SDK/infra tips.

maria: hmm. for (1) we had a similar flake in dedicated where refresh race caused a short window of invalid auth. are you using the sdk built-in token refresh, or rolling your own?

alex: using the ts sdk refresh helper (TokenProvider) but we wrap it with our own queue to avoid concurrent refreshes. code snippet:
```ts
await tokenProvider.getToken();
// then batch send via fetch + Authorization: Bearer ${tok}
```
no explicit retries per-request, only per-batch.

jonathan: try adding per-request 401->refresh+retry with small jitter. sometimes the provider returns a token that isn't yet active if there's clock skew w/ kms service. we also observed that increasing concurrency lowered the incidence.

li: for (2) dims — is there any preprocessing that could add a sentinel token or pad? or are you calling different model variants per item?

alex: same model param used for whole batch. no padding. payloads are plain text. failing items are short strings like "OK" and longer docs. weird.

maria: can you log the raw response length and the model id? also check if one of the clients in the pool is using a different quantized variant (we had a routing rule that sometimes prefers low-ram variants for small reqs).

alex: good call. logging shows model: "open-embedding-v1" for all. response lengths: mostly 1536, a few 1537. attaching sample: 
```
item: "OK"
embedding_len: 1537
first_vals: [0.0123, -0.0045, ...]
```

jonathan: that suggests there's an extra bias term getting appended server-side for some shards. file an infra ticket? @ops-bot can you create a ticket for infra to check model shard output parity?

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-7192 — investigate embedding vector length mismatch for open-embedding-v1. assigned to eng-runtime.

li: about (3) stream extra empty vector — is your stream parser treating a trailing 

alex: yes, our parser assumes any final newline-delimited JSON line is an object. we get a stray "[]" line then parser throws when validating schema. quick fix was to filter out empty arrays, but i'd like to understand origin.

maria: sometimes the server emits an explicit keepalive chunk as "[]" when there's no new tokens, to keep the connection alive. streaming contract should document that, but sdk parsers should ignore empty arrays. looks like ts sdk didn't special-case it.

jonathan: actionable items:
- alex: add per-request 401 retry + token refresh + jitter, and reduce per-batch concurrency for now (quick patch).
- alex: log model id + node id + raw embedding length for bad cases and attach to INF-7192.
- devex (maria): add stream keepalive semantics to the ts sdk parser to ignore [] chunks.
- infra: investigate shard parity (INF-7192).

alex: will do. i'll push a small PR for the retry logic and a parser guard to drop empty arrays. pinging for code review when up.

maria: thx. once you're done, add a unit test for the stream guard (simulate trailing []), and add a short blurb in the sdk changelog.

li: if you want, i can correlate the node_id from logs with current rollout map to see if it's a canary.

alex: yes please, that'd help. i'll attach logs to the ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
